s: Which one of the following was the principal change made by the 2023 Act in relation to the interim mechanism in Anoop Baranwal?
o: The entire Selection Committee was replaced by the Search Committee.
The Prime Minister was replaced by the President.
The Leader of Opposition was replaced by the Law Minister.
The Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
x: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India on the selection panel with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

s: Who formed the interim selection panel directed by the Constitution Bench in Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023)?
o: Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Law Minister and Chief Justice of India
President, Prime Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
x: Until Parliament enacted a law, the Constitution Bench directed selection by a panel comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition or leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India.

s: Who heads the Search Committee for Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act?
x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister, has two Secretary-rank members and shortlists five names.

s: Who set up the Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms?
x: Jayaprakash Narayan set up the Tarkunde Committee, which proposed a three-member Election Commission.

s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, to whom does the Selection Committee recommend names for appointment?
x: The Selection Committee, which may pick names outside the Search Committee's shortlist, recommends names to the President for appointment.

s: What majority does the challenged composition of the Selection Committee under the 2023 Election Commission law give the government?
x: Petitions by ADR and Jaya Thakur challenge the 2:1 government majority; the Supreme Court said the CJI's place had been only temporary, pending a law.

s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, the Search Committee shortlists how many names?
x: The Search Committee, headed by the Law Minister with two Secretary-rank members, shortlists five names.

s: The CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023 (Act No. 49 of 2023) replaced the earlier Act of which year?
x: The 2023 Act replaced the 1991 Act on the service conditions of the CEC and ECs.

s: Who chairs the Selection Committee for the CEC and Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act?
x: The Selection Committee is the PM (chair), the LoP in Lok Sabha and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

s:
Consider the following statements about the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023:
1. The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister.
2. The Selection Committee can choose only from the names shortlisted by the Search Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Law Minister heads the Search Committee, but the Selection Committee may pick names outside its shortlist of five.

s: In which case has the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023 been challenged before the Supreme Court?
o: Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
Jaya Thakur v. Union of India
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
x: ADR and Jaya Thakur challenged the 2023 Act (Jaya Thakur v. Union of India, pending as of May 2026).

s: With whom are the salaries of the CEC and Election Commissioners on a par?
o: a judge of a High Court
a judge of the Supreme Court
x: They are paid on a par with a Supreme Court judge, and their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.

s: On which fund is there a demand that the expenses of the Election Commission of India be charged?
x: Critics note the ECI's dependence on DoPT, Law and Home Ministries and demand its expenses be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

s: Under which Article does the Constitution place post-retirement restrictions on the Comptroller and Auditor General?
x: Article 148(4) bars the CAG from further office after retirement; there is no such express bar for retiring Election Commissioners.

s: How many members' signatures does a motion to remove the Chief Election Commissioner need, if moved in the Rajya Sabha?
x: The removal motion needs at least 100 Lok Sabha members or 50 Rajya Sabha members.

s: Which of the following does the Constitution prescribe for members of the Election Commission?
x: The Constitution provides for appointment by the President but prescribes no qualifications, no term and no post-retirement bar.

s: An Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until attaining what age, whichever is earlier?
x: The ECI has one CEC and two ECs, appointed by the President, each serving six years or until age 65.

s: The removal safeguard for the Chief Election Commissioner is provided under which provision of the Constitution?
x: Article 324(5) protects the CEC: they can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.

s: The head of a State Election Commission can be removed only in the manner of which of the following?
x: A State Election Commissioner is removed like a High Court judge, while the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge.

s: On whose recommendation can the President remove an Election Commissioner from office?
x: ECs and Regional Commissioners can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation.

s: Which of the following is correct about the term of the CEC under the 2023 Act?
o: Five years or age 62, with reappointment allowed
Six years or age 65, whichever is earlier, with no reappointment
Six years or age 65, with one reappointment allowed
Until age 70, with no fixed term
x: The CEC and ECs hold office for 6 years or till 65, whichever is earlier, and cannot be reappointed.

s: Which Article of the Constitution bars the Chairman of the UPSC from further employment under the Government?
x: Article 319 bars the UPSC Chairman (and 148(4) the CAG); the Constitution has no such bar for Election Commissioners.

s: In which year did V.S. Ramadevi, the first woman Chief Election Commissioner of India, serve?
x: V.S. Ramadevi served as CEC in 1990; T.N. Seshan was the tenth CEC.

s: Strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct from 1991 is associated with which Chief Election Commissioner?
x: Strict MCC enforcement (1991), EPIC and removal of partisan police officers belong to the T.N. Seshan era.

s: The Opposition's removal motion against which Chief Election Commissioner was described as the first such motion against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act?
x: The removal motion was moved against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and was described as the first such motion against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act.

s: Which number Chief Election Commissioner of India was T.N. Seshan, whose tenure (1990-96) is known as the reform era?
x: T.N. Seshan was the 10th CEC, from 12 December 1990 to 11 December 1996.

s: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
x: Sukumar Sen was the first CEC (1950-58).

s: Who delivered the first Sukumar Sen Memorial Lecture of the Election Commission in January 2020?
x: The first Sukumar Sen Memorial Lecture was given by Pranab Mukherjee on 23 January 2020.

s: Who was the Chief Election Commissioner in 2000, when T.S. Krishnamurti and J.M. Lyngdoh served as Election Commissioners?
x: M.S. Gill was CEC in 2000; Krishnamurti and Lyngdoh were ECs under him and later became CEC.

s: Who among the following was never a member of the Election Commission of India?
x: N.B. Lohani was not a member of the ECI; the other three served as CEC.

s: Who is the present Chief Election Commissioner of India?
x: Gyanesh Kumar is the present (26th) CEC; Anil Chandra Punetha is AP's State Election Commissioner.

s: Gyanesh Kumar is which Chief Election Commissioner of India by number?
x: Gyanesh Kumar is the 26th CEC; T.N. Seshan was the 10th.

s: Of which States did V.S. Ramadevi, the only woman Chief Election Commissioner, serve as Governor?
x: V.S. Ramadevi, the first and only woman CEC (1990), was Governor of Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh.

s: When may the Election Commission mainly use the reservoir of power under Article 324?
o: A State Election Commission requests it in every case
No law holds the field on the matter concerned
A law already completely occupies the field
The President delegates legislative power to it
x: Article 324 operates as a reservoir where no law holds the field; it cannot ordinarily override an existing law governing the matter.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court describe Article 324 as a 'reservoir of power'?
o: Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
ADR v. Election Commission of India
x: Mohinder Singh Gill (1978) called Article 324 a reservoir of power, usable where no law holds the field.

s: What is the name of the headquarters of the Election Commission of India in New Delhi?
x: The ECI sits at Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi; its training arm is IIIDEM.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners?
o: The CEC and the ECs have equal powers and differences are settled by majority
The CEC has a permanent veto over the decisions of the ECs
The CEC alone takes all substantive decisions of the Commission
The ECs can overrule the CEC only with the President's approval
x: The CEC and the other Election Commissioners have equal powers, and differences are resolved by majority decision.

s: Two Election Commissioners were added in 1989 after which Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18?
x: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18, after which two Election Commissioners were added in 1989.

s: Since when has the Election Commission of India been a multi-member body continuously?
x: The ECI has been a three-member body continuously since 1 October 1993; its members are paid like Supreme Court judges.

s: The constitutional validity of the multi-member Election Commission and the majority rule was upheld in which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
ADR v. Election Commission of India
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
x: The Supreme Court upheld the multi-member structure and majority rule in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995).

s: Whom does the President consult before appointing Regional Commissioners?
x: The President may appoint Regional Commissioners after consulting the Election Commission.

s: Which institute in New Delhi is the training arm of the Election Commission of India?
x: The India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM) is the ECI's training arm.

s: In which Part of the Constitution does Article 324, which provides for the Election Commission of India, lie?
x: Article 324 lies in Part XV (Articles 324-329).

s: The Model Code of Conduct rests on which provision, and applies from when?
o: Article 324; from the announcement of the election schedule
Article 324; from the start of polling
Representation of the People Act, 1951; from the announcement of the schedule
Representation of the People Act, 1951; from the declaration of results
x: The MCC is not a statute; it rests on Article 324 and applies from the announcement of the election schedule (Harbans Singh Jalal, 1997).

s: Who headed the Commission that conducted the 2022 delimitation of Jammu and Kashmir?
x: The J&K delimitation (2022) was done by a Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai, while Assam was delimited by the ECI.

s: Which body decides every step of the election process, from the announcement of the schedule to the declaration of results?
x: The ECI decides every step from announcement to results; Panchayat and municipal polls belong to the State Election Commissions.

s: Under which of the following does the Election Commission recognise political parties and allot election symbols?
x: Party recognition and symbol allotment are governed by the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, issued under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and Article 324.

s: Under which provisions is Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls ordered?
o: Article 280 and Section 21 of the Delimitation Act, 2002
Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Article 243K and Section 11 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
Article 326 and Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
x: Special Intensive Revision is ordered under Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

s: Under which Article does the Election Commission advise the Governor on disqualification of members of State Legislatures?
x: The ECI advises the Governor under Article 192 and the President under Article 103; anti-defection cases go to the Speaker or Chairman.

s: Under which Article does the ECI advise the President on the disqualification of Members of Parliament?
x: Article 103 covers ECI advice to the President on MPs; Article 192 covers advice to the Governor on MLAs.

s: Who decides disqualification on grounds of defection under the Tenth Schedule?
x: Anti-defection cases go to the Speaker or Chairman, not the ECI.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Election Commission of India?
o: Recommending President's Rule in a State
Advising the Governor on disqualification of MLAs
x: Recommending President's Rule is not an ECI function; the others are its administrative, quasi-judicial and advisory roles.

s: Who carried out Assam's delimitation, effective August 2023?
o: Delimitation Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai
x: The ECI itself delimited Assam; the J&K delimitation of 2022 was done by a Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai.

s: In which case was it held that the Model Code of Conduct applies from the day the election schedule is announced?
x: The Harbans Singh Jalal case (1997) held that the MCC applies from the announcement of the schedule.

s: Which part of the Model Code of Conduct deals with the conduct of the party in power?
x: Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct covers the party in power; the MCC rests on Article 324, not a statute.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Lok Sabha Speaker and Deputy Speaker are chosen internally by the Lok Sabha under Article 93.
The Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman is chosen internally under Article 89(2).
The Election Commission of India elects the Chairman of a State Legislative Council under Article 182.
The Assembly Speaker and Deputy Speaker are chosen internally by the Assembly under Article 178.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Legislative Council elects its own Chairman under Article 182. Presiding officers are chosen by their own Houses, not by the ECI.

s: The election of which of the following is conducted by the Election Commission of India?
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
x: The ECI conducts the Vice-President's election; presiding officers of the Houses are chosen by their own Houses.

s: How are the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha chosen?
o: By the Lok Sabha itself under Article 93
x: Under Article 93 the Lok Sabha itself chooses its Speaker and Deputy Speaker; the ECI has no role.

s: Under Article 324(1), to elections of which of the following does the ECI's superintendence NOT extend?
x: Article 324(1) covers Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President; Panchayat and municipal polls come under the State Election Commissions.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: District Collector – District Election Officer/District Returning Officer
Election Commission of India – Conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
State Election Commission – Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
Chief Electoral Officer – Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
x: The Chief Electoral Officer is the State-level officer under the ECI's control; local-body elections are conducted by the State Election Commission.

s: At the district level, who appoints Returning and Presiding Officers?
x: Each State has a Chief Electoral Officer, while at district level the Collector/District Election Officer appoints Returning and Presiding Officers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Chief Electoral Officer is removed like a High Court judge
The State Election Commission functions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer functions under the Representation of the People Act, 1950
The State Election Commissioner is removable only like a High Court judge
x: The Chief Electoral Officer is removed by the Election Commission; only the State Election Commissioner has High Court judge-like protection.

s: Under which Article is the State Election Commission for municipal elections provided?
x: Article 243ZA covers municipal elections; 243K covers Panchayat elections and 324 the ECI.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Anil Chandra Punetha — new State Election Commissioner for local-body polls
Anil Chandra Punetha — first Chief Election Commissioner of India
Gyanesh Kumar — State Election Commissioner for local-body polls in Andhra Pradesh
Sukumar Sen — officer associated with 100% SIR digitalisation in ASR district
x: Anil Chandra Punetha was identified as the new State Election Commissioner for local-body polls. The other pairs wrongly assign unrelated national or district-level roles.

s: Under which provision is the Chief Electoral Officer of a State provided for?
x: The CEO rests on Section 13A of the RPA 1950 and is not a constitutional authority.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Chief Electoral Officer of a State?
o: The ECI appoints the CEO in consultation with the State Government
The CEO is a constitutional authority
The CEO can be removed by the ECI
The CEO oversees Lok Sabha and Assembly polls under ECI control
x: The Chief Electoral Officer is a statutory officer under Section 13A of the RPA 1950, not a constitutional authority.

s: Panchayats are listed in which entry of the State List?
x: Local government (panchayats) is entry 5 of the State List; the State Government decides to hold panchayat elections.

s: Since which year has 25 January been observed as National Voters' Day?
x: National Voters' Day marks the ECI's founding on 25 January 1950 and has been observed since 2011.

s: In which year did the Election Commission of India observe its Diamond Jubilee?
x: The Diamond Jubilee was in 2010; the Golden Jubilee was in 2001 and 75 years were completed in 2025.

s: Which ECI app lets citizens report Model Code of Conduct and expenditure violations with time-stamped evidence?
x: cVIGIL lets citizens report MCC and expenditure violations with time-stamped evidence; status is given within 100 minutes.

s: Whom is the Saksham-ECI app meant mainly to help?
x: Saksham-ECI, developed with the Department of Empowerment of PwDs, gives registration and polling help to persons with disabilities.

s: Which of the following ECI app – purpose pairs is correctly matched?
o: cVIGIL – help for persons with disabilities
SVEEP – home voting for voters above 85
x: The Voter Helpline uses toll-free 1950; cVIGIL is for MCC violations, Saksham-ECI for PwDs and SVEEP for voter education.

s: Above what age is the home-voting facility available to voters?
x: Home voting is for voters above 85 and PwDs with 40% benchmark disability.

s: In April 2019, the Supreme Court raised VVPAT slip verification to how many randomly selected EVMs per Assembly segment?
x: On 8 April 2019 the SC raised verification from one to five randomly selected EVMs-VVPATs per Assembly segment.

s: In ADR v. ECI (April 2024), symbol loading units are to be sealed and kept in the strong room for how many days after results?
x: The SC rejected 100% VVPAT verification and ordered symbol loading units sealed for 45 days after results.

s:
Consider the following statements about the ADR v. ECI judgment (26 April 2024):
1. It ordered 100% VVPAT verification.
2. A verification request must be made within 7 days of results, at the candidate's cost.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only statement 2 is correct; the Supreme Court rejected the demand for 100% VVPAT verification.

s: What is the purpose of SVEEP of the Election Commission of India?
o: Registration help for persons with disabilities
x: SVEEP is the ECI's voter awareness and education programme for inclusive elections.

s: Within how many minutes does a cVIGIL complainant get the status of the complaint?
x: cVIGIL lets citizens report MCC and expenditure violations with time-stamped evidence; status is given within 100 minutes.

s: With which department did the Election Commission develop the Saksham-ECI app?
o: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
x: Saksham-ECI helps persons with disabilities register and vote; it was developed with the Department of Empowerment of PwDs.

s: Persons with disabilities can use home voting if they have a benchmark disability of at least:
x: Home voting is for voters above 85 and persons with 40% benchmark disability.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 71 – Disputes on Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections
Article 329(b) – Bar on questioning delimitation in court
Article 329(a) – Challenge to an election only by election petition
x: Article 71 covers disputes on Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections; 329(a) bars court challenges to delimitation and 329(b) requires an election petition.

s: How must a challenge to an election result be made after it has been declared?
o: A review by the Election Commission
x: The Election Commission cannot review a declared result and does not try election petitions; challenges follow the election-petition route.

s: Which court tries an election petition on a Parliamentary or State Legislature election, and where does the appeal lie?
x: Such election petitions are tried by the High Court, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.

s: Under Section 57 of the RPA 1951, who may adjourn a poll disrupted by riot or open violence?
x: Section 57 lets the Presiding or Returning Officer adjourn the poll; the adjourned poll resumes with ECI approval.

s: Under which Section of the RPA 1951 may the ECI declare a poll void and order a fresh poll if an EVM is unlawfully taken away or tampered with?
x: Section 58 covers EVMs or ballot boxes taken, destroyed, lost or tampered with; Section 57 covers adjournment and 58A booth capturing.

s: Which of the following RPA 1951 section – situation pairs is correctly matched?
x: Section 58A deals with booth capturing; Section 57 with riot or calamity and Section 58 with EVMs taken or tampered with.

s: Who decides disputes relating to the election of the President and Vice-President?
x: Under Article 71, President and Vice-President election disputes go to the Supreme Court.

s: Under which Article can laws on delimitation and allotment of seats not be questioned in any court?
x: Article 329(a) bars courts from questioning delimitation and seat allotment laws.

s: When a poll adjourned under Section 57 of the RPA 1951 resumes, who may vote?
o: All voters on the roll again
Only those who had not voted before the adjournment
Only voters whose names the Observer approves
x: Under Section 57 the adjourned poll resumes with ECI approval, and only those who had not already voted may vote.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Article 325 provides for one general electoral roll and prohibits exclusion on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. Article 324 concerns the Election Commission, Article 326 adult suffrage, and Article 329 court-related bars.

s: What does Article 83, which may need amending for simultaneous elections, deal with?
o: Duration of the Houses of Parliament
x: Articles 83 and 85 concern Parliament's term and sessions, 172 and 174 the States', and 356 President's Rule; all may need amending.

s: Elections to panchayats and municipalities in India are conducted by which body?
o: The Election Commission of India under Article 324
State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer of the State under Article 325
x: Panchayat and municipal polls are run by the State Election Commissions under Articles 243K (panchayats) and 243ZA (municipalities), not by the ECI. Article 324 vests control of Parliament, State legislature, President and VP elections in the ECI; Article 325 provides one general electoral roll; Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters. The CEO and Delimitation Commission do not conduct local polls.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with disqualifications for membership of Parliament?
x: Article 102 covers disqualifications for Parliament; 84 its qualifications, 173 and 191 those for State Legislatures.

s: IIIDEM, which trains election managers, is an institute of which body?
x: IIIDEM belongs to the Election Commission, a permanent independent constitutional body constituted in 1950.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court describe Article 324 as a “reservoir of power”?
o: Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
x: In Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1978), the Supreme Court described Article 324 as a reservoir of power.

s: Under Article 329, how can an election be challenged?
o: A reference to the Election Commission
x: Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters; an election can be questioned only through an election petition.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 171 – Superintendence, direction and control of elections by the Election Commission
Representation of the People Act, 1951 – Conduct of elections and disqualification of members
Representation of the People Act, 1950 – Allocation of seats and preparation of electoral rolls
x: Article 171 deals with the composition of State Legislative Councils; superintendence of elections is vested in the ECI by Article 324.

s: Which Article of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India?
x: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.

s: What does Article 325 of the Constitution provide for?
o: Adult suffrage for Lok Sabha and Assemblies
One general electoral roll for every territorial constituency
A bar on courts in electoral matters
x: Article 325 provides one general electoral roll per constituency with no exclusion on religion, race, caste or sex.

s: Which Part of the Constitution deals with elections (Articles 324-329)?
x: Part XV, Articles 324 to 329, contains the electoral provisions of the Constitution.

s: In which year was the Election Commission of India constituted?
x: The ECI was constituted in 1950 as a permanent, independent constitutional body.

s: Under Article 324(2), who fixes the number of Election Commissioners other than the Chief Election Commissioner?
x: Article 324(2) provides for a CEC and such other Election Commissioners as the President may fix.

s: Which Article of the Constitution lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament?
x: Article 84 gives qualifications for Parliament; Article 102 gives disqualifications; 173 and 191 are the State versions.

s: Under Article 326, on which grounds may a citizen aged 18 or above be disqualified from voting?
o: Non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt practice
x: Article 326 grants adult suffrage subject to disqualifications such as non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime and corrupt or illegal practice.

s: Which is the constitutional authority for conducting State Legislative Assembly elections?
x: Assembly elections are direct, use first-past-the-post and are run by the Election Commission of India.

s: Which Amendment Act lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
x: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age to 18.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The right to vote is a Fundamental Right.
2. The right to contest an election is a statutory right.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The right to vote is statutory, not fundamental; the right to contest is also statutory (Kuldip Nayar, 2006).

s: At which address may an overseas Indian elector enrol in the electoral roll?
o: the address of the Indian embassy in the foreign country
any address selected by the elector
the last place of employment in India only
the address of the Indian passport
x: Under Section 20A of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, an overseas elector may enrol at the address given in the Indian passport.

s: In the Kuldip Nayar case (2006), what did the Supreme Court hold the right to vote to be?
x: Kuldip Nayar held the right to vote statutory, not fundamental.

s: How many seats were contested in the first Lok Sabha general elections?
x: 489 seats were contested in the first Lok Sabha elections; G.V. Mavalankar became the first Speaker.

s: In which Lok Sabha constituency did the 2017 by-poll record a turnout of only about 7 per cent amid violence?
x: The 2017 Srinagar Lok Sabha by-poll was marred by violence and saw a turnout of only about 7.14%.

s: Which of the following pairs (Lok Sabha – year of election) is correctly matched?
x: The 1st, 9th, 11th and 16th Lok Sabhas were elected in 1952, 1989, 1996 and 2014 respectively.

s: In which year was the 17th Lok Sabha elected?
x: The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019; 2014 elected the 16th and 2024 the 18th.

s: How many general elections to the Lok Sabha have been held so far, with the 2024 election included?
x: Eighteen general elections have been held; the 18th Lok Sabha was elected in 2024.

s: Who is regarded as independent India's first voter?
x: Shyam Saran Negi of Kalpa, Kinnaur (Himachal Pradesh) cast the first vote in October 1951.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats were filled in the first general election of 1951-52?
x: The first general election (25 October 1951 – 21 February 1952) was held for 489 seats.

s: Which Article provides one-third reservation of seats for women under the 106th Amendment?
x: Article 334A relates to the women's one-third reservation; Article 330 covers SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha and 331 the former Anglo-Indian nomination.

s: Which Lok Sabha constituency in Andhra Pradesh is reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
x: Araku is the ST-reserved constituency; Amalapuram and Tirupati are SC-reserved.

s: In a constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes, who can vote?
o: Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes
x: Reserved constituencies have a common electorate: all voters, not merely those of the reserved community, may vote.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation under the 106th Amendment?
o: It provides one-third reservation of seats
It operates immediately, irrespective of census and delimitation
x: Its operation begins only after the next census and delimitation.

s: How many seats in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly are reserved for Scheduled Castes?
x: Andhra Pradesh has 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats; Telangana has 19 SC and 12 ST.

s: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies under Article 334 has been extended up to 2030 by which Amendment?
x: The 104th Amendment (Act of 2019, in force January 2020) extended SC/ST seat reservation under Article 334 to 2030 and ended Anglo-Indian nomination. Article 334 originally set 10 years (till 1960). The 95th Amendment gave the previous extension; the 106th introduced one-third women's reservation (Art 334A); the 84th dealt with the delimitation freeze.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats in Telangana are reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
x: Telangana has 2 ST seats (Adilabad, Mahabubabad) and 3 SC seats; Andhra Pradesh has 1 ST seat (Araku).

s: Under Article 333, the Governor could nominate how many Anglo-Indian members to a State Assembly?
x: Article 333 allowed the Governor to nominate one Anglo-Indian; Article 331 allowed two to the Lok Sabha. Both ended with the 104th Amendment.

s: Which of the following Article – provision pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 330 – SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha
Article 332 – SC/ST seats in State Assemblies
Article 331 – Anglo-Indian nomination to State Assemblies
x: Article 331 concerned nomination of two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha; nomination to Assemblies was under Article 333.

s: In which year did the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies come to an end?
x: The 104th Amendment (in force January 2020) extended SC/ST reservation to 2030 but ended Anglo-Indian nomination in 2020.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats in Andhra Pradesh are reserved for Scheduled Castes?
x: AP has 4 SC seats (Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati) and 1 ST seat (Araku) in the Lok Sabha.

s: For how long did Article 334 originally provide reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the legislatures?
x: Article 334 first gave reservation for 10 years (till 1960); later amendments extended it, now till 2030.

s: How many Lok Sabha seats in Telangana are reserved for Scheduled Castes?
x: Telangana has 3 SC Lok Sabha seats: Peddapalle, Warangal and Nagarkurnool.

s: Which of the following Lok Sabha constituencies of Telangana is reserved for Scheduled Castes?
x: Nagarkurnool is an SC seat; Adilabad and Mahabubabad are ST seats.

s: How many seats in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly are reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
x: Of AP's 175 Assembly seats, 29 are reserved for SCs and 7 for STs.

s: Which of the following Lok Sabha constituencies of Andhra Pradesh is NOT reserved for Scheduled Castes?
x: AP's SC Lok Sabha seats are Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor and Tirupati; Nellore is not among them.

s: Which principle underlies the exercise of delimitation?
o: One State, one vote, one value
One district, one representative, one value
One party, one constituency, one value
One person, one vote, one value
x: Delimitation rests on the principle of ‘one person, one vote, one value’, associated with uniformity of representation under Article 81(2).

s: Who heads the Delimitation Commission?
x: It is set up under an Act of Parliament, headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with the CEC and State Election Commissioners as members.

s: In which year was the Delimitation Commission under the Delimitation Act of 1972 constituted?
x: The Delimitation Acts were enacted in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002; the Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.

s: On the basis of which Census did the 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001 permit rationalisation of constituencies?
x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze on inter-State seat allocation and allowed rationalisation using the 1991 Census.

s: Who chaired the Delimitation Commission of 1973?
x: Justice J.L. Kapur chaired the 1973 Commission; Justice Kuldip Singh chaired the 2002 Commission.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution is NOT correct?
o: It proposed freezing the Lok Sabha at 543 seats permanently.
It proposed retaining a 2.2:1 Lok Sabha to Rajya Sabha ratio.
It linked the proposed women’s quota to delimitation from 2029.
It proposed women’s quota from 2029 without linking it to delimitation.
x: The resolution proposed women’s reservation from 2029 without linking it to delimitation. It also proposed a permanent freeze at 543 Lok Sabha seats and retention of the 2.2:1 ratio.

s: What is the present number of elected Lok Sabha seats, and what is the constitutional ceiling?
x: The Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats against a ceiling of 550, comprising 530 seats for States and 20 for Union Territories in the stated allocation framework.

s: Which Article provides for readjustment of State Legislative Assembly constituencies after each census?
x: Article 170 provides for readjustment of Assembly constituencies; Article 82 does so for the Lok Sabha and Article 81(2) embodies uniformity of representation.

s: The freeze on the inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 1971 Census was first imposed by which Amendment, and until when?
x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze inter-State seat allocation on the 1971 Census till 2000 to encourage population control. The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze till the first census after 2026, and the 87th (2003) switched boundary redrawing to the 2001 Census. The 44th Amendment did not deal with the freeze.

s: To what number did the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 propose to raise the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550?
x: The Bill proposed 850 seats with delimitation on the 2011 Census, but it was defeated.

s: What does the increase in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana Assembly seats under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 await?
x: The seat increase under Section 26 awaits the census conducted after 2026.

s: On what basis does delimitation redraw territorial constituency boundaries?
x: Delimitation uses recent census figures so that each seat has roughly equal population, ensuring equal representation.

s:
Assertion (A): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be questioned in court.
Reason (R): Orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be modified by legislatures.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Delimitation Commission orders cannot be challenged in court, and legislatures cannot change them. These are two separate safeguards, so R does not explain A.

s: Under which of the following is the Delimitation Commission constituted?
o: A notification of the Election Commission
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha
An executive order of the President
x: It is constituted under parliamentary legislation, works with the ECI, and its orders cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or Assemblies.

s: Towards which States do Southern States fear population-based delimitation would shift Lok Sabha seats?
x: Population-based delimitation would shift representation towards more populous States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.

s: Which Amendment provided for redrawing constituency boundaries on the 2001 Census, with total seats unchanged?
x: The 87th Amendment (2003) allowed boundary redrawing on the 2001 Census without changing total seats.

s: Which of the following is an ex officio member of the Delimitation Commission under the 2002 Act?
o: The State Election Commissioner of the State concerned
The Governor of the State concerned
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chief Minister of the State concerned
x: Members are a Supreme Court judge (Chairperson), the CEC or an EC nominated by him, and the State Election Commissioner concerned, ex officio.

s: Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides for raising Andhra Pradesh Assembly seats from 175 to how many?
x: Section 26 raises AP seats from 175 to 225 (Telangana 119 to 153), subject to Article 170.

s: Which of the following Amendment – delimitation effect pairs is correctly matched?
o: 84th Amendment – Boundaries redrawn on the 2001 Census
42nd Amendment – Freeze of State seat shares on the 1971 Census
87th Amendment – Freeze till the first census after 2026
x: The 42nd Amendment froze seat shares on the 1971 Census; the 84th extended the freeze till after 2026 and the 87th used the 2001 Census for boundaries.

s: How is the constitutional ceiling of 550 elected Lok Sabha seats made up?
x: The ceiling is 550 (530 States + 20 UTs); the old 552 figure with 2 Anglo-Indians is outdated.

s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014 made follow-up changes to the Representation of the People Act, 1950. What does the RPA, 1950 mainly deal with?
o: Allocation of seats and preparation of electoral rolls
Conduct of elections and election petitions
x: The RPA 1950 is the pre-election framework: allocation of seats and electoral rolls; the RPA 1951 covers conduct of polls, party registration, corrupt practices and petitions.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Delimitation Commission:
1. It fixes the seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
2. Its orders can be modified by the Lok Sabha.
3. The Ministry of Law and Justice is its nodal ministry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Commission fixes SC/ST reserved seats and works under the Law Ministry; its orders have the force of law and cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or Assemblies.

s: Who chaired the Delimitation Commission constituted in 2002?
x: The 2002 Commission was chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh; J.L. Kapur chaired the 1963 and 1973 Commissions.

s: Who chaired the first Delimitation Commission, set up in 1952?
x: The 1952 Commission was chaired by Justice N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar; J.L. Kapur chaired the 1963 and 1973 Commissions.

s: Who headed the Delimitation Commission for Jammu and Kashmir, whose orders were issued in 2022?
x: The J&K Delimitation Commission was chaired by Justice Ranjana Desai; its orders came in 2022.

s: What happened to the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which sought to raise the Lok Sabha ceiling to 850?
o: It was defeated in the Lok Sabha for want of a special majority
It was passed and ratified by half the States
It was referred to the Delimitation Commission
It was struck down by the Supreme Court
x: The Bill got 298 votes for and 230 against, short of the special majority, and was defeated in the Lok Sabha.

s: Under first-past-the-post in Lok Sabha elections, how does a candidate win?
o: At least two-thirds of the valid votes
More than half of the valid votes
At least one-third of the valid votes
x: FPTP needs only a plurality in a single-member constituency, not a majority.

s: The State Legislative Assembly is elected from which type of constituencies?
x: Assembly members are directly elected from single-member territorial constituencies, by first-past-the-post.

s: Which of the following was cited as a reason for rejecting proportional representation for Lok Sabha elections?
o: It guarantees direct election in every single-member constituency
It may lead to unstable governments
It reduces the cost of elections
x: Unstable governments, fragmentation, expense, difficulty for voters and a weaker voter–MP link were cited against PR; guaranteeing direct election in single-member seats is not such a reason.

s: Who elects the Vice-President of India?
x: The Vice-President is elected by all MPs, elected and nominated, by single transferable vote; the President by elected MPs and MLAs.

s: Under which Article is the Vice-President elected?
x: The Vice-President is elected under Article 66; the President under Article 54.

s: Which of the following has no role in the election of the Vice-President of India?
x: The Vice-President is elected only by MPs of both Houses, elected and nominated; State Legislatures have no role.

s: A candidate forfeits the security deposit on securing not more than what share of the valid votes?
x: A candidate with one-sixth or less of the valid votes forfeits the deposit.

s: Which additional areas are included in the Presidential electoral college through the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act?
o: Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
x: The 70th Amendment (1992) added the elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry to the electoral college for the President.

s: A candidate can win a State Assembly election without getting more than 50 per cent of the votes. Which system makes this possible?
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
x: Under first-past-the-post, the candidate with the most valid votes wins even without 50 per cent.

s: By whom are the members of the Rajya Sabha from the States elected?
o: Elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
Members of the State Legislative Councils
All members of the Lok Sabha
x: Rajya Sabha members (Art. 80) are elected by elected MLAs through proportional representation by single transferable vote.

s: What is the minimum age to contest elections to Panchayats and Municipalities?
x: The minimum age to be a member of a Panchayat or Municipality is 21 years.

s: What is an election held after a legislature is dissolved before the end of its normal term called?
x: A mid-term election follows premature dissolution; a by-election fills a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months.

s: In which of the following cases does the six-month rule for holding a by-election NOT apply?
o: The vacancy arises in a reserved constituency
The vacancy arises from the resignation of the member
The vacancy arises during a session of the House
The remaining term is less than one year
x: The exceptions are a remaining term of less than one year, or the Election Commission certifying difficulty after consulting the Central Government.

s: What is a constituency with no fixed geographical boundary, such as the Sangha seat in Sikkim, called?
x: A floating constituency has no fixed geographical boundary. The Sangha constituency in Sikkim is an example in which only registered Buddhist monks vote and contest.

s: The Model Code of Conduct rests on the Election Commission's plenary power under which Article?
x: The Model Code is a set of ECI guidelines supported by Article 324, not a statute enacted by Parliament.

s:
Arrange the following milestones relating to the Model Code of Conduct in chronological order:

A. Part VII relating to the party in power was added
B. The Code was first drafted by the Kerala Government
C. The Code was revised
D. The Code was formalised by the Election Commission

Select the correct sequence.
x: The sequence is 1960 drafting by Kerala, 1968 formalisation by the ECI, 1974 revision, and 1979 addition of Part VII.

s: In which State's 1960 Assembly election was the Model Code of Conduct first drafted and used?
x: The Code was first used in Kerala in 1960, formalised by the ECI in 1968 and strictly enforced by T.N. Seshan in 1991.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a restriction under Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Introducing new schemes or grants after announcement of polls
Using official machinery or transport for campaigning
Continuing ordinary official visits without combining them with electioneering
x: Part VII (party in power) bars combining official visits with electioneering, using official machinery or transport, and announcing new schemes or grants once polls are announced (options A, B, C). Ordinary official visits not combined with electioneering are not restricted, so D is the answer.

s: Under which provision can the Election Commission suspend or withdraw the recognition of a political party for violating the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968
x: Sanctions for MCC violations range from censure up to suspension or withdrawal of recognition under Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. Section 29A deals with party registration, Section 126A with exit polls, and Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters.

s: When does the Model Code of Conduct come into force?
o: Immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule by the ECI
After the completion of nomination and scrutiny
After Parliament approves the election schedule
When the election results are declared
x: The Model Code of Conduct takes effect as soon as the ECI announces the election schedule, and lasts until the results.

s: What is the legal status of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Election Commission guidelines not enacted by Parliament
x: The MCC is a set of ECI guidelines, not a statute; its authority comes from Article 324.

s: In which case was it held that the Model Code of Conduct comes into force from the announcement of the election schedule?
o: Kuldip Nayar v Union of India
Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India
x: Harbans Singh Jalal v UoI (1997, Punjab and Haryana HC) held the MCC applies from the announcement of the schedule.

s: Which Chief Election Commissioner strictly enforced the Model Code of Conduct from 1991?
x: The Model Code was strictly enforced from 1991 under CEC T.N. Seshan.

s: The 'Sahulat' app, launched to facilitate voting, was associated with which of the following?
o: Jammu and Kashmir, for elderly voters
Sikkim, for Buddhist monks in the Sangha seat
x: The Sahulat app was a Jammu and Kashmir initiative for elderly voters (APPSC 2019). Meghalaya was the first State to provide Braille-enabled ballot papers at all booths; overseas electors enrol under Sec 20A at their passport address; the Sangha seat in Sikkim is a floating constituency. None of these is the Sahulat app.

s: How may persons in preventive detention vote?
o: A special booth in the jail
x: Persons in preventive detention, along with service voters, special voters and electors on election duty, are covered by postal-ballot provisions.

s: What is the age threshold for senior citizens in the absentee-voter postal ballot category?
x: The senior-citizen threshold is 85 years or above, raised from 80 years.

s: Which of the following ECI initiative – purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: SVEEP – Voter education and electoral participation
cVIGIL – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Saksham – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Voter Helpline – Registration, corrections, roll search and complaints
x: cVIGIL is for reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos; Saksham assists voters with disabilities.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Voter Helpline app — Search name in electoral roll
ECINET — Exclusive platform for election petitions
x: ECINET is a unified platform merging more than 40 Election Commission applications and websites; it is not an exclusive platform for election petitions.

s: The bar on opinion polls during the 48 hours before the close of poll is provided under which Section of the RPA, 1951?
x: Section 126 bars opinion polls in the 48 hours before the close of poll; Section 126A governs the longer restriction on exit polls.

s: Who built the NETA app, which lets voters rate their elected representatives?
o: The Ministry of Law and Justice
x: The NETA app was built by a private start-up; it was not conceptualised by the Election Commission of India.

s: What does the cVIGIL app of the Election Commission let citizens do?
o: Report Model Code violations with geo-tagged photos or videos
Help elderly voters in Jammu and Kashmir
x: cVIGIL reports MCC violations, with action within 100 minutes; NETA rates representatives, Sahulat helps J&K elderly voters and Saksham serves voters with disabilities.

s: Which was the first State to provide Braille-enabled ballots at all polling booths?
x: Meghalaya was the first State with Braille-enabled ballots at all booths (APPSC 2018).

s: Under SVEEP, the voter education programme of 2009, with which organisation did the Election Commission partner?
x: The ECI partnered Indian Railways under SVEEP for voter awareness (APPSC 2019).

s: Section 126A of the RPA, 1951 bars exit polls from the start of polling in the first phase till when?
o: Half an hour after the last phase closes
48 hours before the close of poll
One hour after the first phase closes
x: Section 126A bars exit polls until half an hour after the last phase; the 48-hour bar under Section 126 is for opinion polls.

s: Within how many minutes is action promised on a complaint made through the cVIGIL app?
x: cVIGIL lets citizens report Model Code violations with geo-tagged photos or videos, with action within 100 minutes.

s: What is ECINET of the Election Commission of India?
o: A single platform joining more than 40 ECI apps and websites
An app for reporting Model Code violations
A network of observers for expenditure
A portal for filing election petitions
x: ECINET brings 40+ ECI apps and websites onto one platform; cVIGIL is the app for MCC complaints.

s: Which of the following statements about NOTA in Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections is incorrect?
o: NOTA continues to be applicable in these elections because they are indirect elections.
NOTA is not applicable in Rajya Sabha elections.
NOTA is not applicable in Legislative Council elections.
The Supreme Court struck down NOTA in these elections in 2018.
x: Option A is incorrect: the Supreme Court struck down NOTA for Rajya Sabha and Council elections in 2018. NOTA applies only to direct Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.

s: Which of the following describes an Electronic Voting Machine?
o: A judicial mechanism for resolving election disputes
An electoral system based on proportional representation
An electronic vote recording and counting apparatus
x: An EVM is a machine that records and counts votes. It is not an electoral system; first-past-the-post is the system.

s: NOTA is NOT applicable in which of the following elections?
x: NOTA does not apply to Rajya Sabha or Legislative Council elections.

s: What did a voter do under the old Rule 49-O?
o: Entered the booth but refused to vote before the Presiding Officer
Voided the result by majority rejection
Pressed the NOTA button on the EVM
x: Old Rule 49-O meant refusing to vote before the presiding officer; NOTA means pressing a button on the EVM.

s: Former Rule 49-O was struck down because a voter's refusal to vote was recorded in which Form, breaking secrecy?
x: Recording the refusal in Form 17-A broke the secrecy of the vote.

s: The indelible election ink used in India is manufactured by which organisation and is based on which substance?
o: Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd; silver nitrate
x: Indelible election ink is manufactured by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd and is based on silver nitrate.

s: In which general election was indelible ink first used in India?
x: Indelible ink was first used in the 1962 general election. The claim that it was first used in Mysore in 1960 is incorrect.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court direct a NOTA option on all Electronic Voting Machines?
o: Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India, 1997
Mohinder Singh Gill v Chief Election Commissioner, 1978
Kuldip Nayar v Union of India, 2006
x: In PUCL v Union of India on 27 September 2013, the Supreme Court directed that a NOTA button be provided on all EVMs.

s: Who designed the NOTA symbol, a ballot paper with a black cross?
o: The National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad
x: The NOTA symbol was designed by NID Ahmedabad; it was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NOTA first used in a Lok Sabha general election – 2013
x: VVPAT was first used at Noksen in 2013; EVMs were first used at Parur in 1982 and NOTA in a Lok Sabha general election in 2014.

s: To which Article did the Supreme Court link the right to cast a secret negative vote (NOTA)?
x: The Court linked a secret negative vote to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).

s: Which of the following statements regarding NOTA is incorrect?
o: A fresh poll is not automatically held merely because NOTA receives the maximum votes.
The contesting candidate with the highest valid votes is declared elected even when NOTA has the maximum votes.
NOTA is a symbolic expression only.
NOTA automatically invalidates the election whenever it receives more votes than every candidate.
x: Option D is incorrect: NOTA is only symbolic. Even if it tops the count, the candidate with the most votes wins and no fresh poll is held.

s:
Consider the following statements about NOTA:
1. Exercising NOTA is active participation in the electoral process.
2. NOTA is equivalent to abstention.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Using NOTA is voting, by registering a negative choice; it is not the same as abstaining.

s: Where was an Electronic Voting Machine first used in India, in 1982?
x: EVMs were first used at Parur in Kerala in 1982; Noksen saw the first VVPAT in 2013.

s: In N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India (2019), VVPAT slips were to be tallied in how many polling stations per Assembly segment?
x: The 2019 ruling raised the VVPAT tally from one to five polling stations per Assembly segment.

s:
Consider the following statements about ADR v ECI (2024):
1. The Supreme Court rejected 100% VVPAT slip counting.
2. Second- and third-placed candidates may seek checks of 5% of EVMs per constituency.
3. Such a request must be made within 30 days of the results.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the written request must be made within 7 days of results, not 30.

s: On which finger of the voter is indelible election ink applied?
x: Indelible ink, made by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd, is applied on the left forefinger.

s: What is the key chemical in the indelible ink used in Indian elections?
x: Silver nitrate is the key chemical; the formula comes from the National Physical Laboratory and it is applied on the left forefinger.

s: Where was VVPAT first used in 2013?
x: The first VVPAT use was at Noksen, Nagaland, in 2013.

s: What happens if NOTA receives the highest number of votes in a constituency?
o: The candidate with the most votes is still declared elected
The Election Commission nominates a member
x: NOTA is symbolic: even if it gets the most votes, the top candidate wins and there is no fresh poll.

s: Which institution developed the formula of the indelible ink used in Indian elections?
x: The formula was developed by the National Physical Laboratory; the ink is made by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd.

s: What is the minimum age for a citizen to contest a Lok Sabha election?
x: A Lok Sabha candidate must be a citizen on the electoral roll of a constituency and at least 25 years old.

s: Which of the following governs the recognition of political parties and reservation of symbols?
x: The 1968 Order recognises parties and reserves symbols; the RPA 1950 covers seats and rolls, and the RPA 1951 nomination, scrutiny and counting.

s:
Which of the following statements are correct?
I. The RPA, 1950 is connected with Articles 81, 82, 170, 171, 325 and 326.
II. The RPA, 1951 is connected with Articles 84, 102, 173, 191, 324 and 329.
III. Article 329 is listed as a constitutional connection of the RPA, 1950.
x: I and II are correct: the RPA, 1950 links to Articles 81, 82, 170, 171, 325 and 326, and the 1951 Act to 84, 102, 173, 191, 324 and 329. III is false because Article 329 belongs with the 1951 Act.

s: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the disqualification for conviction continues for how long after release?
x: Under the RPA 1951 the disqualification continues for six years after release. Three, five and ten years are distractors.

s: Election expense accounts are dealt with in which Sections of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
x: Sections 77–78 of the 1951 Act cover election expenses; Section 8 covers disqualifications.

s: Under Section 78 of the RPA 1951, within how many days must election expense accounts be filed with the District Election Officer?
x: Section 78 requires expense accounts to reach the DEO, usually the Collector, within 30 days.

s: Who issues the notification for a Lok Sabha general election under Section 14 of the RPA 1951?
x: The President notifies Lok Sabha polls on the ECI's recommendation; the ECI fixes the schedule and nomination dates.

s: Which of the following deals with corrupt practices in elections?
x: Corrupt practices and disqualifications are in the RPA, 1951; voter registration is in the 1950 Act.

s: Who issues the notification for a State Assembly general election under Section 15 of the RPA, 1951?
x: The Governor notifies Assembly polls (Section 15) and the President Lok Sabha polls (Section 14); the ECI never issues the notification.

s: Which of the following deals with the preparation of electoral rolls?
x: RPA 1950 covers the pre-election framework including electoral rolls; RPA 1951 covers actual conduct of elections.

s: Which type of revision rebuilds the electoral roll comprehensively?
x: A Special Intensive Revision rebuilds the electoral roll, whereas summary revision is conducted annually.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the qualifying dates for revision of electoral rolls?
x: The four qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. 1 December is not a qualifying date.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the election machinery?
o: Booth Level Officers now carry standard photo identity cards
The Chief Electoral Officer assists the Election Commission in each State or UT
Electoral Registration Officers and Booth Level Officers are associated with electoral rolls
The Election Commission has no control over officers deployed on poll duty
x: The Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.

s: Which of the following is a category of observer appointed by the Election Commission under Section 20B?
x: Section 20B observers are general, police and expenditure observers; there is no judicial observer.

s: Which officer conducts the poll in a constituency and declares the result?
x: The Returning Officer conducts the poll and declares the result; the DEO, usually the Collector, receives expense accounts.

s: Who usually acts as the District Election Officer?
x: The District Election Officer is usually the Collector; candidates file expense accounts with the DEO.

s: In which State did the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision remove about 70 lakh names from the electoral roll?
x: The Supreme Court let the ECI's Bihar SIR go ahead; it removed about 70 lakh names.

s: For State party recognition on seat share, a party needs three per cent of Assembly seats or how many seats, whichever is more?
x: One alternative criterion is three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more.

s: In at least how many States must a party be recognised as a State party to qualify as a National Party?
x: State-party recognition in four or more States is one of the alternative criteria under the Election Symbols Order, 1968.

s: Recognition of political parties under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 is distinct from registration under which provision?
o: Section 19 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
x: Recognition is governed by the Election Symbols Order, 1968, whereas registration of political parties is under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

s: Who registers political parties under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951?
x: Section 29A of the RPA, 1951 empowers the Election Commission of India to register political parties.

s: How many recognised national parties were there in 2025?
x: In 2025 there were six national parties: BJP, INC, BSP, CPI(M), AAP and NPP.

s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised national party (2025)?
x: TMC, NCP and CPI lost national status; the six national parties are BJP, INC, BSP, CPI(M), AAP and NPP.

s: How many registered unrecognised political parties did the Election Commission delist for non-compliance?
x: The ECI delisted 808 registered unrecognised parties; over 2,800 RUPPs exist in all.

s: The grounds for declaring an election void are listed in which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
x: Section 100 lists grounds such as disqualification of the returned candidate, corrupt practice and improper rejection of a nomination.

s: From 1 July 2024, where are electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation found?
x: From 1 July 2024 these offences are in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (Sections 169–177); earlier they were in IPC Chapter IXA.

s: Within what period should the High Court try to decide an election petition?
x: The High Court should try to decide an election petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.

s: Trial of election petitions by the High Court is provided in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
x: Section 80A provides for trial by the High Court; Section 81 prescribes the 45-day filing limit.

s: Who decides disputes relating to the election of the President and Vice-President?
x: Under Article 71, Presidential and Vice-Presidential election disputes go to the Supreme Court, not the ECI.

s: Under Section 81 of the RPA, 1951, an election petition must be filed within how many days of the returned candidate's election?
x: Section 81 sets a 45-day limit for filing an election petition.

s: Which court tries election petitions under the RPA, 1951?
x: Under Section 80A, election petitions are tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court.

s: The rule that no election can be called in question except by an election petition is in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
x: Section 80 bars questioning an election except by petition; Section 81 is the 45-day limit.

s: Where does an appeal against a High Court decision on an election petition lie?
x: Election petitions are tried by the High Court, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.

s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for declaring an election void under Section 100 of the RPA, 1951?
o: A corrupt practice by the candidate
The returned candidate was not qualified
The returned candidate won by a very small margin
x: Section 100 grounds are disqualification, corrupt practice, improper rejection of nomination and improper acceptance of votes affecting the result; a narrow margin is not a ground.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms?
o: It was appointed in 1974 and reported in 1975
It was set up by Jayaprakash Narayan
It proposed a selection panel of the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
It recommended a three-member Election Commission and a voting age of 18
x: The proposed panel was the PM, the Leader of the Opposition and the CJI, not the Speaker.

s: Which Law Commission report recommended giving the ECI a limited power to deregister non-compliant parties?
x: The 255th Report (2015) sought limited deregistration power; the 170th Report (1999) dealt with internal party democracy and partial list seats.

s: In which year was the Dinesh Goswami Committee on electoral reforms set up?
x: The Goswami Committee dates from 1990; 1993 is the Vohra Committee on the crime-politics nexus.

s: Which one of the following committees/commissions was NOT concerned with Centre-State relations?
x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with state funding of elections (an electoral reform), so it is the odd one out (APPSC-G2 2025, UPPSC 2015). The Rajamannar Committee (Tamil Nadu, 1969-71), Sarkaria Commission (1983-88) and Punchhi Commission (2007-10) all examined Centre-State relations.

s: Who recommended the use of 'totalisers' in counting votes?
x: The Law Commission's 255th Report (2015) recommended totalisers, which pool the count of several control units so booth-wise voting patterns stay hidden. The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with state funding, the Vohra Committee with the crime-politics nexus, and the 2nd ARC with ethics in governance.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sarkaria Commission – Recommendation for a permanent Inter-State Council
Indrajit Gupta Committee – State funding of elections
Rajamannar Committee – State-level initiative for federal autonomy
Punchhi Commission – State-level initiative for federal autonomy
x: Punchhi dealt with federal dialogue and coordination mechanisms; the State-level autonomy initiative was Rajamannar (Tamil Nadu).

s: Which of the following was recommended by the Dinesh Goswami Committee?
o: Allocation of State Legislative Council seats
A selection panel of PM, LoP and CJI
x: The Goswami Committee recommended EVMs and State funding, leading to the 1996 RPA amendment; Council seat allocation was not its subject.

s: Barring candidates upon framing of charges in serious offences was recommended by which Law Commission report?
x: The recommendation was made in the Law Commission's 244th Report of 2014.

s: What did the Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommend on electoral reform?
o: Full state funding and a lifetime ban on convicted legislators
Simultaneous elections and a constructive no-confidence motion
Partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences
x: The Second ARC recommended partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences.

s: Who set up the Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms (1974-75)?
x: The Tarkunde Committee was set up by JP; it proposed a 3-member ECI and voting age 18.

s: Who chaired the Second Administrative Reforms Commission, which reported on 'Ethics in Governance'?
x: The 2nd ARC (2007-09) under Veerappa Moily recommended partial State funding.

s: Which committee of 2013 recommended barring candidates charged with sexual offences from contesting elections?
x: The J.S. Verma Committee (2013) on criminal-law reform recommended barring candidates charged with sexual offences.

s: Which Law Commission report of 1999 recommended simultaneous polls and internal democracy in political parties?
x: The 170th Report (1999) backed simultaneous polls, internal party democracy and some list seats.

s: What is a totaliser, which combines the counting of several EVMs, meant to do?
x: A totaliser combines several EVM counts to hide booth-wise trends; the ECI stated no legal framework for it exists.

s: Where is ECIL, one of the two public sector undertakings that make EVMs, headquartered?
x: BEL is based in Bengaluru and ECIL in Hyderabad.

s: Under ADR v. ECI (2024), for how long are symbol-loading units to be sealed and kept?
x: The Court rejected ballot papers and 100% VVPAT counting, but ordered SLUs preserved for 45 days and allowed runners-up to seek checking of 5% of EVMs.

s: Which case held that VVPAT is necessary for free and fair elections and directed its introduction in phases?
o: State of Karnataka v Prathik Parasrampuria
x: In Subramanian Swamy v ECI (2013), the Supreme Court held that VVPAT was needed for free and fair polls and required phased introduction.

s: In ADR v ECI (2024), how did the Supreme Court respond to the demand to return to paper ballots?
o: Ordered a return to paper ballots
Refused to order a return to paper ballots
x: The Supreme Court refused to order a return to paper ballots and has repeatedly upheld the use of EVMs.

s: How did N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India (2019) change the random VVPAT-EVM tally?
o: Two to five polling stations per district
One to five polling stations per Assembly segment
One to ten polling stations per parliamentary constituency
Five to ten polling stations per Assembly segment
x: The 2019 decision raised the random VVPAT-EVM tally from one to five polling stations per Assembly segment.

s: VVPAT slips must be counted in which of the following circumstances?
o: Whenever EVM data and Form 17C do not match
Whenever postal ballots exceed the number of EVM votes
Only in constituencies using postal ballots
Only when the winning candidate requests it after the declaration of results
x: VVPAT slips are required to be counted wherever the EVM data and Form 17C do not match.

s: Which State was the first to conduct its entire Assembly election using EVMs?
x: Goa conducted the first whole-State Assembly election using EVMs in 1999. Gujarat was not the first State to do so.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: VVPAT was introduced on 4 September 2013; EVMs were first used on 19 May 1982, EPIC rolled out in 1993 and NOTA on 27 September 2013.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Goa (1999) – First State-wide Assembly election using EVMs
Parur Assembly Constituency – First experimental use of EVM
14th Lok Sabha election (2004) – First nationwide general election entirely using EVMs
x: VVPAT was first introduced in Noksen Assembly Constituency; Goa saw the first all-EVM State poll.

s: An M3 EVM control unit can connect up to how many ballot units?
x: An M3 system can take up to 24 ballot units (384 candidates including NOTA), whereas M2 supports four ballot units and 64 candidates.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about VVPAT?
o: The slip is handed over to the voter for personal custody
It prints a slip with the serial number, name and symbol of the selected candidate
The voter can see the printed slip for seven seconds
It is attached to the Electronic Voting Machine
x: The voter only views the slip through the VVPAT window; it is not handed over.

s: What is the principal purpose of a Remote Voting Machine (RVM) prototype?
o: To permit domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station
To count postal ballots together with EVM votes
To enable overseas citizens to vote in all constituencies without registration
To conceal booth-wise voting patterns by pooling control units
x: The ECI's RVM prototype is intended to enable domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station.

s: At how many electors per polling station did the Election Commission fix the cap?
x: The ECI capped the number of electors per polling station at 1,200, down from the earlier 1,500.

s:
Which of the following is the correct order of counting-related procedures?
A. Counting of postal ballots
B. Counting of the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round
C. Counting of the final EVM/VVPAT round
x: Postal ballots are counted before the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round; the final EVM/VVPAT round follows subsequently.

s:
Consider the following statements about EVMs:
1. They were first used at Parur, Kerala, in 1982.
2. Gujarat was the first State to hold its entire Assembly election on EVMs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only statement 1 is correct: Goa (1999), not Gujarat, was the first whole-State Assembly poll on EVMs.

s: An M3 EVM control unit can handle up to how many candidates, including NOTA?
x: One M3 control unit takes 24 ballot units, i.e. 384 candidates including NOTA; the M2 took 64.

s: For how long is a VVPAT slip visible to the voter through the window?
x: The VVPAT slip is shown for 7 seconds and is not handed to the voter.

s: The 2004 election to the 14th Lok Sabha was the first of which of the following?
o: National election held entirely on EVMs
x: 2004 was the first all-EVM national election; VVPAT and NOTA came in 2013.

s: A Remote EVM (RVM) can handle up to how many constituencies from one remote polling station?
x: The RVM, for domestic migrants, can cover up to 72 constituencies from one remote station.

s: How many candidates can an M2 EVM with four ballot units handle?
x: An M2 EVM takes 4 ballot units, that is 64 candidates; an M3 control unit takes 24 ballot units, or 384 candidates including NOTA.

s: Which case arose from the first use of EVMs at Parur (Kerala) in 1982?
o: N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India
x: The 1982 Parur EVM trial was challenged in A.C. Jose v Sivan Pillai; Section 61A then gave EVMs statutory backing in 1989.

s: Which two public sector undertakings manufacture EVMs in India?
x: EVMs are made by Bharat Electronics Ltd (Bengaluru) and Electronics Corporation of India Ltd (Hyderabad).

s: In which year was NOTA first used in a Lok Sabha election?
x: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections; its first Lok Sabha use was in 2014.

s: In which year was the Electors' Photo Identity Card (EPIC) introduced?
x: EPIC was introduced in 1993 and its number stays valid for life despite a change of address; it did not come through the 61st Amendment.

s: Which law provided for linking electoral rolls with Aadhaar to check multiple enrolment?
o: Representation of the People Act, 1950 as originally enacted
x: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 provided Aadhaar linking, multiple qualifying dates, gender-neutral wording and requisition of premises.

s: Who make up the selection panel under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023?
o: The Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Union Home Minister
The Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition
The President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition
x: The 2023 Act provides for a panel comprising the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. The Chief Justice of India was dropped from the panel.

s: Under which Chief Election Commissioner was the nationwide rollout of Electors Photo Identity Cards started in 1993?
x: The nationwide EPIC rollout began in 1993 under Chief Election Commissioner T.N. Seshan.

s: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections of which of the following States?
x: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly polls of Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.

s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, who was dropped from the selection panel?
x: The 2023 Act panel is the PM, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM and the LoP; the CJI was dropped.

s:
Arrange the following electoral reforms in chronological order:
1. Statutory backing to EVMs through Section 61A
2. Introduction of EPIC
3. Cap of two constituencies per candidate
4. Aadhaar linking of electoral rolls
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Section 61A came in 1989, EPIC in 1993, the two-seat cap in 1996 and Aadhaar linking by the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021.

s: Who was the Chief Election Commissioner when the ECI and State Election Commissions signed a declaration in February 2026 to share EVMs, rolls and ECINET?
x: The ECI-SEC declaration of 26 February 2026 was made under CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh achieved 100% digitisation of Special Intensive Revision forms in July 2026?
x: Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) district completed 100% digitisation of SIR forms in July 2026.

s: Which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 bans exit polls?
x: Section 126A of the RPA, 1951 concerns the ban on exit polls.

s: A candidate forfeits the security deposit when the candidate fails to secure more than which proportion of the total valid votes polled?
x: A candidate loses the security deposit if they win no more than one-sixth of the valid votes.

s: Under Section 33(7) of the RPA, 1951, from how many constituencies at most can a candidate contest a Lok Sabha or Assembly election?
x: Section 33(7), added in 1996, limits a candidate to two constituencies.

s: Disclosure of criminal antecedents of candidates is dealt with in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
x: Section 33A concerns disclosure of criminal antecedents; Section 8 is disqualification, 29A registration and 123 corrupt practices.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the corrupt practices covered by Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Failure to file an election expenditure account within 30 days
Appeal on the grounds of religion or caste
