x: Section 123 covers corrupt practices such as bribery, undue influence and appeals based on religion or caste. Filing the expenditure account within 30 days is governed by Section 78.

s: Within how many days must a person elected from two constituencies vacate one of them?
x: Under Section 70 one seat must be vacated within 14 days; the two-constituency cap in Section 33(7) came with the 1996 amendment.

s: Which Section of the RPA, 1951 requires a candidate to keep an account of election expenses?
x: Section 77 requires the account to be kept; Section 78 requires it to be filed with the DEO within 30 days.

s: Under Section 34 of the RPA 1951, what is the security deposit for a general-category Lok Sabha candidate?
x: It is ₹25,000 for the Lok Sabha and ₹10,000 for an Assembly; SC/ST candidates pay half.

s: What does Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 relate to?
o: Corrupt practices during an election campaign
The maintenance of election expenditure accounts
Election petitions presented in the High Court within 45 days of the result
x: Section 81 concerns election petitions, which are presented in the High Court within 45 days of the election result.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Section 135B — Liquor ban for 48 hours before polling
Section 135C — Paid holiday on polling day
Section 70 — Disqualification under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
x: Section 151A concerns holding a by-election within six months. Section 135B provides for a paid holiday, Section 135C concerns the liquor ban, and Section 70 deals with vacating one of two seats.

s: Section 61A was inserted into the Representation of the People Act, 1951, in which year to provide statutory backing to Electronic Voting Machines?
x: Section 61A was added to the RPA, 1951 in 1989 to give EVMs legal backing, after the 1982 trial was challenged.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RPA, 1951:
1. Under Section 70, a person elected from two seats must vacate one within 14 days.
2. Under Section 81, an election petition must be filed within 30 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only statement 1 is correct: Section 81 allows 45 days; 30 days is the limit for filing expense accounts under Section 78.

s: Under Section 34 of the RPA, 1951, what is the security deposit for a general-category Assembly candidate?
x: The deposit is ₹10,000 for Assembly and ₹25,000 for Lok Sabha; SC/ST candidates pay half.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the death of a contesting candidate?
o: The election is automatically cancelled in every case of the death of a candidate.
The death of a candidate no longer automatically countermands the election.
The change was made through the 1996 Amendment.
Recognized political parties may nominate a replacement within a set timeframe.
x: Option A is incorrect: since the 1996 amendment, a candidate's death no longer cancels the election automatically. A recognised party can name a replacement within a set time.

s: Which problem does the reform principle 'one candidate, one seat' address?
o: Candidates contesting from more than one constituency
x: The Law Commission proposed 'one candidate, one seat' for candidates contesting from more than one constituency; the ECI proposed the vacating candidate bear by-election costs.

s: Which one of the following was a major provision of the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 1996?
o: Removal of the limit on constituencies from which a candidate may contest
Reduction of security deposits and proposers for independent candidates
Abolition of by-elections within six months
Capping a candidate’s contest to two constituencies and increasing security deposits
x: The 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies, increased security deposits, and required more proposers for independents and unrecognised parties.

s: The 1996 two-constituency cap followed the 1991 election. Who contested from three Lok Sabha seats in that election?
x: The 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies after Devi Lal stood from three Lok Sabha seats in 1991.

s:
Assertion (A): A registered elector in India can contest a Rajya Sabha election from any State.
Reason (R): The 2003 Amendment removed the requirement that the candidate be an elector in the particular State.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: since a 2003 amendment removed the rule that a candidate must be a voter in that State, any registered voter in India can contest a Rajya Sabha seat from any State. R explains A.

s: The ban on liquor sale for 48 hours before a poll, added in 1996, is in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
x: Section 135C bans liquor; 135B gives a paid holiday and 151A requires by-polls within 6 months.

s: What was the main reason why the most Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held in the 1990s?
x: Unstable minority and coalition governments in the 1990s led to frequent elections.

s: Under Section 8 of the RPA 1951, conviction with imprisonment of how long or more leads to disqualification?
x: Section 8 disqualifies on conviction with two years' imprisonment or more; Lily Thomas removed protection during pendency of an appeal.

s: For a political party to retain tax exemption under the stated provisions, which combination is relevant?
o: No donation above ₹2,000 in any form and no record of larger donations
No cash donation above ₹20,000 and records only of donations above ₹2,000
No cash donation above ₹2,000 and proper records of donations above ₹20,000
Acceptance of unlimited cash donations provided they are reported after the election
x: The stated conditions include no cash donation above ₹2,000 and maintenance of records for donations above ₹20,000. These are referred to under Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, replacing the earlier reference to Section 13A of the 1961 Act.

s: According to ADR, about what share of political parties' funds in 2004-23 came from undisclosed sources?
x: ADR found that 60% (₹19,083 crore) of party funds in 2004-23 came from undisclosed sources.

s: Under which Section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 do political parties get tax exemption?
x: Party tax exemption is now in Section 12 of the Income-tax Act, 2025; earlier it was Section 13A of the 1961 Act.

s: In ADR v Union of India (2024), on what main ground did the Supreme Court strike down the Electoral Bond Scheme?
o: The right to equality under Article 14
The voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a)
The right to life under Article 21
The freedom of association under Article 19(1)(c)
x: The five-judge bench unanimously held that donor anonymity violated voters' right to information, part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). Articles 14, 21 and 19(1)(c) were not the ground stated for striking the scheme down.

s: The Supreme Court's decision in Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India also invalidated which change associated with electoral political funding?
o: Abolition of political party registration under the RPA
Removal of the corporate donation cap under the Companies Act
Compulsory disclosure of all cash donations by parties
Restriction on donations by individual citizens
x: The Court struck down the removal of the corporate donation cap from the Companies Act.

s: A political party could encash electoral bonds only if it had secured at least what percentage of votes in the last election?
x: Only a registered political party that had secured at least 1% of the votes in the last election could encash electoral bonds.

s: In the 2024 electoral bond judgment, whom did the Supreme Court direct to give donor data to the Election Commission?
x: A five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously struck down the scheme and directed SBI to provide donor data to the ECI.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about electoral bonds?
o: They were sold only by the State Bank of India
They were issued in denominations from ₹1,000 to ₹10 crore
x: The denominations ran from ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore, not ₹10 crore; SBI was the only seller and the bearer bonds were valid for 15 days.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 2013 — Lily Thomas judgment striking down Section 8(4) of the RPA
2002 — Disclosure of criminal record, assets and education
x: Electoral bonds were struck down by the Supreme Court in 2024; they were not introduced in that year. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: Who could buy electoral bonds?
o: Only companies listed on a stock exchange
A citizen of India or a body incorporated in India
x: Bonds could be bought by a citizen of India or a body incorporated in India, alone or jointly.

s: On which date was the Electoral Bond Scheme notified?
x: The scheme was notified on 2 January 2018 and struck down on 15 February 2024.

s: By which bench was the 2024 electoral bonds verdict in ADR v Union of India delivered?
x: A five-judge bench unanimously held the scheme unconstitutional.

s: Through which law was the Electoral Bond Scheme brought in?
x: The Electoral Bond Scheme was notified on 2 January 2018 on the basis of the Finance Act, 2017.

s: Why is Section 77 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 criticised in the context of party expenditure?
o: Prohibits all expenditure on election campaigns
Places a ceiling only on the expenditure of candidates, not on the election expenditure incurred directly by political parties
Places a ceiling only on political parties, not on candidates
Requires all campaign expenditure to be incurred in cash
x: The perceived loophole is that Section 77 caps candidate expenditure while not imposing a comparable ceiling on the parties’ own election spending.

s: What is the current election expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State?
x: The limit is ₹95 lakh (earlier ₹70 lakh), raised by the Conduct of Elections (Amendment) Rules, 2022; ₹40 lakh is the Assembly limit.

s: What is the current election expenditure limit for an Assembly candidate in a larger State?
x: Assembly candidates in larger States may spend ₹40 lakh (earlier ₹28 lakh); ₹95 lakh is the Lok Sabha limit.

s: What is the expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a smaller State or UT?
x: Smaller States/UTs have a Lok Sabha limit of ₹75 lakh (earlier ₹54 lakh).

s: Candidate expenditure limits are prescribed under Rule 90 of which of the following?
x: Limits are fixed under Rule 90, Conduct of Election Rules 1961, raised by the 2022 Amendment Rules.

s: By which of the following were candidate expenditure limits raised to ₹95 lakh (Lok Sabha) and ₹40 lakh (Assembly) in larger States?
x: Limits under Rule 90 of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961 were raised by the Conduct of Elections (Amendment) Rules, 2022.

s: Simultaneous Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held from 1951-52 up to which year?
x: Simultaneous polls were held from 1951-52 to 1967; both the 170th Law Commission Report and the 2018 draft report backed them.

s: Who chaired the High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections (2023-24)?
x: Former President Ram Nath Kovind chaired it; Amit Shah and N.K. Singh were members, and Dinesh Goswami headed the 1990 electoral reform committee.

s: Within how many days of simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly polls did the Kovind High-Level Committee recommend local-body elections?
x: The committee recommended Lok Sabha and Assembly polls together first, followed by local-body elections within 100 days.

s: A proposed safeguard for maintaining governmental accountability under simultaneous elections is based on which model?
o: The Westminster model of an unelected executive
The American model of judicial review
The German model of a constructive vote of no-confidence
x: The proposed safeguard is a constructive no-confidence motion modelled on the German system.

s: What does Article 356, named in the simultaneous-elections debate, deal with?
o: Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner
x: Article 356 concerns President's Rule; Article 83 is duration of Houses of Parliament and Article 174 dissolution of State Legislatures.

s: Which Article is NOT among those the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes to amend?
x: The Bill proposes amendments to Articles 83, 172 and 327, not Article 280.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024?
o: It seeks to synchronise Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections and inserts a new Article 82A
It raises the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850 and inserts Article 334A
It provides one-third reservation for women and amends Article 330
It extends the delimitation freeze beyond 2026 and amends Article 81
x: The 129th Amendment Bill (introduced December 2024, referred to a JPC) aims at simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly elections (APPSC 2024 key); it inserts Art 82A and amends Arts 83, 172 and 327. Raising the ceiling to 850 was the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026; women's reservation (Art 334A) came via the 106th Amendment; the delimitation freeze was extended by the 84th Amendment.

s: Which of the following was a member of the Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections?
x: Members included Amit Shah, Ghulam Nabi Azad, N.K. Singh, Subhash C. Kashyap, Harish Salve and Sanjay Kothari.

s: Which new Article does the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 propose to insert?
x: The Bill inserts Article 82A and amends Articles 83, 172 and 327.

s: To which body was the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill referred in December 2024?
x: The Bill was sent to a JPC in December 2024, which was still examining it in February 2026.

s: In what form did the Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) recommend State funding of elections?
o: Partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates
Full funding in cash to every candidate
Full funding in kind to every candidate
Partial cash funding to independents only
x: It suggested partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates; the recommendation is still not adopted.

s: On which condition did the Law Commission's 170th Report find full State funding of elections desirable?
o: Only recognised parties were allowed to contest
Parties were barred from taking funds from other sources
Independent candidates were excluded from funding
x: The Law Commission considered full state funding desirable only if parties were barred from receiving funds from other sources.

s: The 'level field for resource-poor candidates' argument for State funding of elections rests on equality under which Article?
x: The level-field argument rests on equality under Article 14; curbing black money is another argument in favour, while the fiscal burden is an argument against.

s: According to the Supreme Court decision in State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), eliminating black money from elections is primarily whose core responsibility?
x: The Supreme Court described elimination of black money from elections as a core responsibility of the Election Commission of India.

s: What is the State funding model called in which the State bears all legitimate costs and private donations are banned?
x: Bearing all legitimate costs while banning private donations describes full funding; funding may be full or partial, in cash or in kind.

s:
Consider the following statements about State funding of elections:
1. Germany, Sweden, Japan and Canada practise it.
2. Under full State funding, private donations are banned.
3. The Indrajit Gupta Committee's recommendation was adopted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Indrajit Gupta Committee's recommendation of partial funding was not adopted.

s: Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, subject to which limitation?
o: Approval by the President in all cases
A referendum among members of the House
Approval by the Election Commission before every decision
x: The Speaker or Chairman decides disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, but the decision remains subject to judicial review, as recognised by the Supreme Court in 1992.

s: The judgment in Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) is associated with which of the following conclusions?
o: Disqualification of legislators was transferred from Parliament to the Election Commission.
Only a sitting legislator can be disqualified after a three-month period.
A convicted legislator remains protected until the disposal of the appeal.
A convicted legislator is disqualified immediately, without protection during the pendency of an appeal.
x: The Lily Thomas judgment held that conviction leads to immediate disqualification and that an appeal does not provide protection against that disqualification.

s: In which case was mandatory disclosure by candidates of criminal cases, assets, liabilities and education laid down?
o: Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India
Lily Thomas v. Union of India
Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
x: ADR (2002) made such disclosure mandatory; PUCL placed the voter's right to know in Article 19(1)(a).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about judgments on criminalisation of politics?
o: In Public Interest Foundation (2018), the Court itself imposed disqualification on framing of charges
Public Interest Foundation (2018) ordered publicity of candidates' criminal records
Public Interest Foundation (2018) left disqualification on framing of charges to Parliament
Lily Thomas removed protection from disqualification during pendency of an appeal
x: The Court did not itself impose disqualification on framing of charges; it left the issue to Parliament.

s: Under the ECI's rule, parties fielding candidates with criminal records must publish the details of those records and what else?
o: An undertaking to resign if convicted
The reasons for selecting such candidates
x: Parties must publish the criminal-record details and the reasons for selecting such candidates; withdrawal is not required.

s: How many special courts have been set up for criminal cases involving MPs and MLAs?
x: 12 special courts have been set up for MP/MLA cases, while a PIL seeking a lifetime ban on convicted legislators is pending.

s: The expression 'bahubali culture' in electoral politics refers to the loss of trust in legislatures through what?
x: The expression refers to the use of muscle power and its adverse effect on trust in legislatures.

s: In PUCL v Union of India (2003), the Supreme Court struck down which Section of the RPA, 1951?
x: PUCL (2003) upheld the voter's right to know under Article 19(1)(a) and struck down Section 33B.

s: Lily Thomas v Union of India (2013) struck down which provision of the RPA, 1951?
x: Lily Thomas struck down Section 8(4), the three-month appeal buffer, making disqualification immediate on conviction.

s: In Public Interest Foundation v Union of India (2018), what did the Supreme Court do on disqualifying candidates once charges are framed?
o: Made it a ground under Section 8
Directed the ECI to bar such candidates
x: The five-judge bench did not disqualify on framing of charges and left it to Parliament, but required parties to publish criminal records.

s: Which High Court ruled in 2004 that persons in jail, who have no right to vote, cannot contest elections?
x: The Patna High Court so ruled in 2004 and the Supreme Court upheld it in 2013; Parliament then amended the RPA to let detained persons contest.

s: According to ADR, what share of Lok Sabha MPs elected in 2024 faced serious criminal charges?
x: ADR data show MPs with serious charges rose from 14% (2009) to 31% (2024); 29% is the figure for MLAs.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that hiding serious criminal cases vitiates a candidate's nomination?
o: Ramesh Dalal v Union of India
Lily Thomas v Union of India
Kuldip Nayar v Union of India
x: In Krishnamurthy v Sivakumar (2015) the Court held that concealing serious cases vitiates the nomination.

s: The Communist Party of India formally took shape at which conference?
x: Although the CPI dates its initial association with M.N. Roy and others at Tashkent in 1920, it was formally established at the Kanpur conference in 1925.

s: When was the Republican Party of India, planned by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, formed?
o: during the Constituent Assembly period in 1950
after the formation of the BSP in 1984
x: The Republican Party of India was planned by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and formed after his death in 1956–57.

s: Who founded the Bahujan Samaj Party in 1984?
x: Kanshi Ram founded the BSP (1984); Mulayam Singh Yadav founded the Samajwadi Party (1992).

s: Which of the following pairs (Party – Founder) is correctly matched?
o: Bharatiya Jana Sangh – Syama Prasad Mookerjee
x: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh was founded by Syama Prasad Mookerjee (1951); the DMK by C.N. Annadurai and the Swatantra Party by C. Rajagopalachari.

s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The BJP was formed in 1980 and succeeded the BJS.
II. The BSP was formed in 1984.
III. The Samajwadi Party was formed in 1998.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: I and II are correct: the BJP was formed in 1980 as the Jana Sangh's successor, and the BSP in 1984. III is false because the Samajwadi Party was formed in 1992; 1998 is the Trinamool Congress.

s: The YSRCP emerged in 2011 from a split in which party?
x: The YSRCP emerged from a Congress split in 2011; the TDP was founded by NTR in 1982.

s: In which year was the Communist Party of India founded?
x: The CPI dates from 1925; the CPI(M) emerged after the 1964 split.

s: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
x: W.C. Banerjee was the Congress's first president; Syama Prasad Mookerjee founded the Jana Sangh and Vajpayee was the BJP's first president.

s: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
x: A.O. Hume is identified as the founder of the Indian National Congress, which was established in 1885.

s: In which year was the All India Trinamool Congress formed?
x: The TMC was formed in 1998; the SP dates from 1992, the NCP from 1999 and the BSP from 1984.

s: Who founded the Swatantra Party in 1959?
x: Rajagopalachari founded Swatantra; Narendra Dev, JP and Lohia were Socialist Party leaders.

s: Where was the Samajwadi Party founded in 1992?
x: Mulayam Singh Yadav founded the SP at Lucknow on 4 October 1992.

s: Who founded the DMK in 1949?
x: C.N. Annadurai founded the DMK in 1949, out of Periyar's Dravidar Kazhagam.

s:
Consider the following statements about political parties:
1. The Samajwadi Party is a recognised national party.
2. The Republican Party of India was formed after Dr B.R. Ambedkar's death.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only statement 2 is correct: the RPI was planned by Ambedkar and formed after his death; the SP is not a national party.

s: Who founded the Nationalist Congress Party in 1999 along with P.A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar?
x: Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar formed the NCP on 10 June 1999 after leaving the INC over Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin.

s: In which year was the Aam Aadmi Party founded by Arvind Kejriwal?
x: Arvind Kejriwal founded the AAP in 2012; it became a national party in 2023.

s: Who among the following was a leader of the Socialist Party?
x: Socialist Party leaders included J.P. Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia and Acharya Narendra Dev; Rajagopalachari founded Swatantra.

s: From which organisation did C.N. Annadurai's DMK emerge in 1949?
x: The DMK came out of Periyar's Dravidar Kazhagam in 1949.

s: Over which issue were Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar removed from the Congress before they formed the NCP in 1999?
x: They were removed from the INC after objecting to Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin, and formed the NCP on 10 June 1999.

s: In which year was the Bharatiya Jana Sangh founded by Syama Prasad Mookerjee?
x: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh was founded on 21 October 1951 in Delhi.

s:
Arrange the following parties in chronological order of formation:
1. Swatantra Party
2. Bharatiya Janata Party
3. Telugu Desam Party
4. Bahujan Samaj Party
In which year did N.T. Rama Rao form the Telugu Desam Party?
x: The TDP was formed by NTR in 1982, between the BJP (1980) and the BSP (1984).

s: Which of the following parties was formed earliest?
x: Forward Bloc (1939) came before the DMK (1949), Jana Sangh (1951) and Swatantra (1959).

s: Which of the following parties was formed after the Janata Dal (1988)?
x: The Samajwadi Party was formed in 1992; the BSP (1984), TDP (1982) and BJP (1980) came earlier.

s: On which date did the Communist Party of India complete 100 years of its foundation?
x: The CPI marked its 100th foundation day on 26 December 2025.

s: With which subject is the Vohra Committee (1993) associated?
x: The Vohra Committee (1993) dealt with the criminalisation of politics.

s: What are pressure groups described as?
x: Pressure groups, which seek influence rather than power, are called the 'Anonymous Empire'.

s: Periodic internal elections to choose a party's office-bearers are a feature of which of the following?
x: Inner-party democracy means periodic elections within the party to choose its office-bearers.

s: Who was the first Andhra to become President of the Indian National Congress?
x: P. Anandacharyulu presided over the 1891 Nagpur session, the first Andhra to head the INC.

s: In which year did P. Anandacharlu, the first Andhra to become INC President, preside over the Congress session?
x: P. Anandacharlu presided over the 7th INC session at Nagpur in 1891.

s: At which place was the Congress session presided over by P. Anandacharlu in 1891 held?
x: Anandacharlu was President of the 1891 Nagpur session, the 7th session of the INC.

s: In which year was the Kamaraj Plan introduced?
x: Under the Kamaraj Plan (1963) senior Congress ministers resigned to work for the party.

s: After whose death did the AIADMK split from the DMK?
x: The AIADMK broke away after the death of C.N. Annadurai, not Karunanidhi.

s: With reference to the split in the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) in 2023, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Sharad Pawar faction retained the NCP name, and the Ajit Pawar faction formed the NCP-SP
The Ajit Pawar faction retained the NCP name, upheld by the top court, and the Sharad Pawar group formed the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar)
Both factions merged into the Indian National Congress
The Election Commission froze the NCP name and neither faction could use it
x: In the 2023 split the Ajit Pawar faction kept the NCP name, which the top court upheld, while Sharad Pawar's group became the NCP-SP (Sharadchandra Pawar). Option A reverses the factions; there was no merger with the INC and the name was not frozen.

s: Into which two parties did the Indian National Congress split in 1969?
x: The Congress split of 1969 produced Congress (Organisation) and Congress (Requisitionists), commonly abbreviated as Congress (O) and Congress (R).

s: Which of the following groups merged to form the Janata Party in 1977?
o: Congress (O), Jana Sangh, BLD and Socialists
Jana Sangh, CPI(M), Congress (S) and Lok Dal
Congress for Democracy, NCP, BLD and Socialists
x: The Janata Party was formed in 1977 through the merger of Congress (O), Jana Sangh, the Bharatiya Lok Dal and the Socialists.

s: Which groups came together to form the Janata Dal on 11 October 1988?
o: Congress(R), Janata Party, CPI and Lok Dal
Jan Morcha, Congress(S), Janata and Lok Dal
Jan Morcha, Congress(O), DMK and Socialists
Congress(O), Jana Sangh, BLD and Socialists
x: The Janata Dal was formed on 11 October 1988 through the merger of Jan Morcha, Congress(S), Janata and Lok Dal.

s: Which of the following is NOT a party of the Janata Dal family?
x: The Janata Dal family includes the RJD, JD(U), JD(S) and BJD; the TDP was formed by NTR in 1982.

s: Who formed the Congress for Democracy in 1977?
x: Jagjivan Ram, with H.N. Bahuguna and Nandini Satpathy, formed the Congress for Democracy in 1977.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: N. Chandrababu Naidu is associated with the Telugu Desam Party, not the Samajwadi Party. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was secretary of the Andhra Communist Party formed in 1936 at which place?
x: Sundarayya was secretary of the Andhra Communist Party at Kakinada (1936).

s: Where did the Justice Party hold its first Andhra session in 1917?
x: The first Andhra session of the Justice Party was held at Pikkavolu in East Godavari in 1917.

s: Who was elected BJP national president unopposed on 20 January 2026?
x: Nitin Nabin, aged 45, succeeded J.P. Nadda as the youngest BJP national president.

s: Since when has Mallikarjun Kharge been president of the Indian National Congress?
x: Kharge became INC president in October 2022, the first non-Gandhi in 24 years.

s: With which party is Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao associated?
x: Harisarvottama Rao led the Andhra Swaraj Party (1934); Madduri Annapurnayya was Forward Bloc and Sundarayya the Andhra Communist Party.

s: With which party was Madduri Annapurnayya of Andhra associated?
x: Madduri Annapurnayya was a Forward Bloc leader; Harisarvottama Rao led the Andhra Swaraj Party.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding election symbols is correct?
o: Recognised parties receive reserved symbols, whereas registered unrecognised parties and independents choose from the free symbols list.
Only national parties are allotted reserved symbols.
Registered unrecognised parties cannot contest elections using any symbol.
Recognised parties and independents must choose symbols from the same reserved-symbol list.
x: Recognised parties receive reserved symbols. Registered unrecognised parties and independents choose symbols from the free symbols list.

s: Which of the following is NOT a stated route for recognition as a State party?
o: Securing 8 per cent of votes alone
Securing 10 per cent of votes alone
Securing 6 per cent of votes and two Assembly seats
Securing 6 per cent of votes in a Lok Sabha election and one Lok Sabha seat
x: The stated vote-only threshold is 8 per cent, not 10 per cent. The other three alternatives are recognised routes.

s: Which is the first national party from the North-East?
x: The National People's Party was the first national party from the North-East; AAP got national-party status in 2023.

s: What share of votes alone can make a party a recognised State party?
x: The vote-only threshold for State party status is 8%, not 10%.

s: On which symbols do registered unrecognised parties and independents contest elections?
x: Recognised parties get reserved symbols; RUPPs and independents get free symbols (184 in May 2025).

s: Within what period of its formation must a party apply for registration under Section 29A of the RPA 1951?
x: The application must be made within 30 days of formation.

s: Which Amendment inserted the Tenth Schedule, through which political parties entered the Constitution?
x: Parties were not in the original Constitution; they entered it via the Tenth Schedule added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold about the Election Commission in INC v Institute of Social Welfare (2002)?
o: Can deregister any party for non-compliance
Cannot ordinarily deregister a political party
Can deregister a party for not contesting elections
x: The ECI cannot deregister a party except in cases of fraud or where the party is declared unlawful.

s: Above what amount must political parties disclose their donors every year?
x: Donors above ₹20,000 are disclosed annually; ₹2,000 is the cap above which donations must be by cheque or bank transfer.

s: The electoral bond scheme was struck down in which case and on what date?
o: ADR v. Union of India, 15 February 2023
PUCL v. Union of India, 15 February 2024
Common Cause v. Union of India, 15 February 2024
ADR v. Union of India, 15 February 2024
x: The electoral bond scheme was struck down in ADR v. Union of India on 15 February 2024.

s: Under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951, to which principles, besides the Constitution, must a party pledge allegiance?
x: A party applying under Section 29A pledges allegiance to the Constitution, socialism, secularism, democracy and national integrity.

s: How must donations above ₹2,000 to a political party be made?
o: In cash through the party treasurer
In cash deposited with the ECI
x: Donations above ₹2,000 may be made only by cheque or bank transfer; ₹20,000 is the disclosure threshold.
